events.text:
This is your goal, add this to documentation / to do lists and push to github You are working on my Avance PD / Avance Work Companion app.

Goal:
Add a new "Health & Outdoors" module that helps Josh stay healthier while working ICT MSP shifts at Avance on Mondays and Wednesdays, usually 8:30am–5:00pm.

Context:
This is not a medical app and must not diagnose, prescribe, or store sensitive medical records. It is a gentle wellbeing-support module for desk-based ICT/MSP work.

Use research-backed themes:
- outdoor light and nature exposure
- hydration reminders
- 20-20-20 eye breaks
- posture and movement breaks
- short active microbreaks
- lunch away from screen
- nervous-system downshift after intense tickets
- end-of-day shutdown ritual
- reducing late screen overstimulation

Use Josh’s personal context:
- ADHD
- screen-heavy MSP work
- tendency to overfocus
- needs gentle prompts, not shame
- wants practical reminders during Monday/Wednesday Avance shifts
- wants outdoor time and body reconnection
- values Christian faith, calm, presence, and family sustainability
- wants no client names, passwords, IPs, hostnames, screenshots, or ticket data stored

Before coding:
1. Inspect the existing repo structure.
2. Identify whether this is:
   - AvancePD: React + TypeScript + Vite, app in src/
   - AvanceProfessionalDevelopment: Next.js app under /app
3. Produce a short implementation plan.
4. Do not delete or rewrite unrelated features.
5. Keep all data local-first unless explicitly implementing an optional email backend.
Prompt 2 — Add the main Health & Outdoors page
Implement a new "Health & Outdoors" page/module.

Requirements:
1. Add a navigation item called "Health & Outdoors".
2. Create a page with these sections:
   - Today’s Shift Health Plan
   - Next Recommended Break
   - Hydration
   - Outdoor / daylight time
   - Eyes and posture
   - Nervous-system reset
   - End-of-day downshift
   - Weekly nature target

The UI should feel calm, low-pressure, and practical.

Core copy style:
- Warm
- Brief
- Not guilt-based
- No medical claims beyond general wellbeing
- Use phrases like:
  "Tiny reset"
  "Step outside if possible"
  "Drink water"
  "Look into the distance"
  "Relax your jaw and shoulders"
  "This is about sustainability, not perfection"

Use cards, progress indicators, and simple action buttons:
- Done
- Snooze 15 min
- Skip for now
- Too busy / urgent ticket

Persist data locally:
- completedBreaks
- skippedBreaks
- hydrationCount
- outdoorMinutes
- lastBreakTime
- notificationPermissionStatus
- preferredReminderCadence
- mondayWednesdayOnly setting

Do not store sensitive health data or client data.
Prompt 3 — Build the Monday/Wednesday shift reminder engine
Build a local reminder schedule engine for Josh’s Avance shifts.

Default shift days:
- Monday
- Wednesday

Default shift time:
- 8:30am to 5:00pm

Default reminder schedule:
- 8:20am: pre-shift setup — fill water, quick daylight, breathe, choose focus
- 9:20am: 20-20-20 eye break + water
- 10:30am: 5-minute outdoor reset if possible
- 11:30am: posture, jaw, shoulders, water
- 12:30pm: lunch away from screen
- 2:15pm: outdoor walk or sunlight reset
- 3:30pm: water + stretch + eyes
- 4:45pm: end-of-day shutdown: notes, tickets, breathe, leave work at work

Rules:
1. Reminders should only trigger on Monday and Wednesday by default.
2. Allow user to enable other days manually.
3. Allow reminder times to be edited.
4. Allow snooze: 15, 30, 60 minutes.
5. If the user marks "urgent ticket mode", reduce reminders to quiet mode for 60 minutes.
6. Persist settings in localStorage or existing app storage.
7. Never block the app or interrupt workflow aggressively.

Add helper function:
getNextHealthReminder(now, settings, completions)

Add unit-safe or simple testable logic where possible.
Prompt 4 — Browser notifications and quiet mode
Add browser notification support for the Health & Outdoors module.

Requirements:
1. Add a "Enable health reminders" button.
2. Request notification permission only after a user click.
3. If permission is granted, show local browser notifications for due reminders.
4. If permission is denied, show in-app reminder banners instead.
5. Use Notification API carefully and progressively.
6. Include a fallback for browsers that do not support notifications.
7. Do not spam notifications.
8. Never ask for notification permission repeatedly after denial.

Notification examples:
- "Tiny reset: drink water and look outside for 20 seconds."
- "Step outside if possible: 5 minutes of daylight can help your body reset."
- "Shoulders down, jaw soft, breathe slowly. Then return to the next ticket."
- "Lunch reset: eat away from the screen if you can."
- "End-of-day: close loops, note next actions, and let work stay at work."

Add settings:
- notificationsEnabled
- quietModeUntil
- reminderSound: false by default
- mondayWednesdayOnly: true by default

Do not implement push server infrastructure yet unless required.
Keep this as local browser notifications first.
Prompt 5 — Health research card library
Add a small research-backed "Why this helps" card library inside Health & Outdoors.

Create cards for:
1. Nature exposure
2. 120 minutes outside per week
3. Microbreaks for fatigue and wellbeing
4. Hydration and clearer thinking
5. 20-20-20 eye rule
6. Movement after sitting
7. Morning/daylight and circadian rhythm
8. Lunch away from screen
9. Nervous-system reset after stressful tickets
10. End-of-day shutdown ritual

Each card should include:
- title
- plain-English summary
- practical action
- sourceLabel
- sourceUrl
- confidenceLevel: strong / moderate / emerging
- category: outdoors / hydration / eyes / movement / stress / sleep

Tone:
- No hype.
- No miracle claims.
- Avoid saying "proven" unless very clear.
- Use "associated with", "may help", "supports", "is linked with".

Example card:
Title: "Nature helps your system downshift"
Summary: "Research links nature exposure with lower stress markers and better mental wellbeing."
Action: "Step outside for 5–10 minutes, look at trees/sky, and let your eyes focus far away."

Store this as static data, not fetched remotely.
Prompt 6 — Personalised MSP health workflow
Integrate Health & Outdoors with the Avance Workday page/dashboard.

Add a "Healthy MSP Shift" panel to the dashboard.

Panel should show:
- current shift state: before shift / morning / lunch / afternoon / wrap-up / off shift
- next health action
- water count today
- outdoor minutes today
- last eye break
- quiet mode status
- quick button: "I’m in urgent ticket mode"
- quick button: "I need a 2-minute reset"

Add a 2-minute reset modal:
Steps:
1. Put both feet on the floor.
2. Relax jaw and shoulders.
3. Breathe slowly.
4. Look away from the screen.
5. Name the next tiny action.
6. Optional: short prayer prompt — "Lord, give me wisdom, patience, and peace."

Important:
- The prayer prompt must be optional and not forced into every reminder.
- Make the module useful in a professional workplace context.
- Keep it private and local.
Prompt 7 — Email reminder option
Design, but do not overbuild, an optional email reminder system.

Problem:
A static local-first web app cannot reliably send scheduled emails by itself. Email reminders need either:
- a backend endpoint,
- Google Apps Script,
- Gmail automation,
- or a scheduled service.

Task:
Add an "Email Reminder Setup" section that explains the options clearly.

Implement Phase 1:
- User can copy recommended reminder schedule as text.
- User can export a .ics calendar reminder file OR copy Google Calendar event text.
- User can copy a Gmail/Google Apps Script prompt for email reminders.
- No API keys in browser.
- No Gmail credentials in the app.
- No real email sending from the frontend.

Add copyable email reminder examples:
Subject: "Avance health reset"
Body: "Drink water, step outside if possible, relax shoulders, then return to the next ticket."

Add future-ready architecture notes in docs:
- /api/send-health-reminder could be added later
- must use server-side secrets only
- must not expose tokens in client code
Prompt 8 — Weekly health review and evidence pack integration
Add a Weekly Health Review section.

Purpose:
Help Josh notice patterns without becoming obsessive.

Track only simple local wellbeing actions:
- total water check-ins
- outdoor minutes
- number of movement breaks
- eye breaks
- lunch away from screen count
- end-of-day shutdown count
- urgent ticket mode count
- skipped reminders

Add reflection prompts:
- "What helped me stay calm this week?"
- "When did I overfocus?"
- "Did I get outside on Avance days?"
- "What reminder was most useful?"
- "What should be gentler next week?"

Add Evidence Pack integration:
Include a manager-safe optional summary like:
"Josh used a structured wellbeing routine to support sustainable MSP work, including planned breaks, hydration prompts, screen breaks, and end-of-day shutdown habits."

Important:
- Do not mention private health diagnoses in manager-safe output unless user manually adds them.
- Do not include personal medical notes.
- Keep export text professional.
Prompt 9 — Accessibility, mobile, and low-friction UX polish
Polish the Health & Outdoors module for accessibility and low cognitive load.

Requirements:
1. Mobile-friendly layout.
2. Large tap targets.
3. High contrast.
4. Clear headings.
5. No cluttered dashboards.
6. No red failure states for missed health actions.
7. Use calm neutral language for skipped reminders.
8. Use "reset" not "failure".
9. Add keyboard-accessible buttons.
10. Add reduced-motion friendly UI.

Add empty states:
- "No reminders due. Keep going steadily."
- "You skipped this one. That’s okay — next tiny reset is enough."
- "Off shift today. You can still choose a gentle outdoor reset."

Add a settings page/section:
- shift days
- shift start/end
- reminder cadence
- notification permission
- enable/disable faith prompt
- enable/disable email setup
- reset health data
- export health data JSON

Make sure existing app styling remains consistent.
Prompt 10 — Final QA, build, and deployment checklist
Do a careful QA pass for the new Health & Outdoors module.

Check:
1. App builds successfully.
2. No TypeScript errors.
3. No console errors.
4. Navigation works.
5. Health & Outdoors page loads.
6. LocalStorage persistence works.
7. Reminder schedule correctly targets Monday and Wednesday 8:30am–5:00pm.
8. Notifications only request permission after a user gesture.
9. Denied notifications fall back to in-app banners.
10. Snooze works.
11. Quiet mode works.
12. Reset/export settings work.
13. No client data or sensitive health data is stored.
14. Existing MSP Skills, Scenarios, Ticket Notes, Evidence Pack and Micro-Learning still work.
15. Mobile layout is usable.

After QA:
- Summarise files changed.
- Summarise new features.
- List known limitations.
- List future improvements.
- Confirm exact build command used.

Do not claim email sending works unless it has actually been implemented and tested with a backend or automation.

- 10 cards covering evidence-based wellbeing:
  1. Nature exposure and nervous system downshift
  2. 120 minutes outdoor time per week
  3. Microbreaks reduce fatigue
  4. Hydration and cognition
  5. 20-20-20 eye rule
  6. Movement breaks after sitting
  7. Morning daylight and circadian rhythm
  8. Lunch away from screen
  9. Nervous-system reset after intense work
  10. End-of-day shutdown ritual

Status: implemented and build-verified.

The Health & Outdoors module adds local-first wellbeing support for Josh's Monday and Wednesday Avance MSP shifts, normally 8:30am-5:00pm. It is intentionally not a medical app: it does not diagnose, prescribe, or store sensitive medical records.

## Implemented Scope

- Sidebar navigation item: `Health & Outdoors`
- Main page: `src/pages/HealthOutdoors.tsx`
- Shared dashboard/workday panel: `src/components/HealthyMspShiftPanel.tsx`
- Local storage and reminder logic: `src/utils/healthOutdoors.ts`
- Static research card data: `src/data/healthResearch.ts`
- Documentation: `docs/HEALTH_AND_OUTDOORS.md`

## User-Facing Features

- Today's Shift Health Plan
- Next Recommended Break
- Hydration check-ins
- Outdoor/daylight minute tracking
- Eyes and posture prompts
- Nervous-system reset with optional faith prompt
- End-of-day downshift
- Weekly nature target
- Weekly Health Review
- Manager-safe Evidence Pack summary text
- Email Reminder Setup with copyable schedule, calendar text, and Google Apps Script prompt

## Reminder Defaults

Default shift days are Monday and Wednesday. Default shift time is 8:30am-5:00pm.

- 8:20am: pre-shift setup
- 9:20am: 20-20-20 eye break and water
- 10:30am: outdoor reset if possible
- 11:30am: posture, jaw, shoulders, water
- 12:30pm: lunch away from screen
- 2:15pm: outdoor walk or sunlight reset
- 3:30pm: water, stretch, eyes
- 4:45pm: end-of-day shutdown

The schedule can be edited in the Health & Outdoors settings section. Other shift days can also be enabled manually.

## Local Data Stored

Data is stored in browser localStorage under `avance-health-outdoors`.

The app stores simple wellbeing action data only:

- completedBreaks
- skippedBreaks
- hydrationCount
- outdoorMinutes
- movementBreaks
- eyeBreaks
- lunchAwayFromScreenCount
- shutdownCount
- urgentTicketModeCount
- lastBreakTime
- snoozedUntil
- notificationPermissionStatus
- preferredReminderCadence
- mondayWednesdayOnly
- notificationsEnabled
- quietModeUntil
- reminderSound

The app must not store client names, passwords, IP addresses, hostnames, screenshots, copied ticket text, private medical notes, or other sensitive operational data.

## Notification Behavior

- Browser notification permission is requested only after the user clicks `Enable health reminders`.
- If permission is granted, local browser notifications can be shown for due reminders.
- If permission is denied or unsupported, the app uses in-app banners.
- Reminder sound defaults to off.
- Quiet mode pauses reminders for 60 minutes during urgent ticket work.

## Email Reminder Design

No email is sent from the frontend. Phase 1 provides copy/export helpers only.

Future email sending would require a backend or automation service, such as:

- `/api/send-health-reminder`
- Google Apps Script
- Gmail automation
- a scheduled service

Any future implementation must keep secrets server-side and must not expose Gmail credentials or API tokens in client code.

## Build Verification

Command used:

```bash
npm run build
```

Result: TypeScript and Vite production build pass.

## Known Limitations

- Email reminders are not sent automatically.
- Notifications are local browser notifications only, not push server notifications.
- Browser notification behavior depends on browser permission settings.
- Health data is local to the current browser profile unless manually exported.

# Health & Outdoors Implementation

Status: implemented and build-verified.

The Health & Outdoors module adds local-first wellbeing support for Josh's Monday and Wednesday Avance MSP shifts, normally 8:30am-5:00pm. It is intentionally not a medical app: it does not diagnose, prescribe, or store sensitive medical records.

## Implemented Scope

- Sidebar navigation item: `Health & Outdoors`
- Main page: `src/pages/HealthOutdoors.tsx`
- Shared dashboard/workday panel: `src/components/HealthyMspShiftPanel.tsx`
- Local storage and reminder logic: `src/utils/healthOutdoors.ts`
- Static research card data: `src/data/healthResearch.ts`
- Documentation: `docs/HEALTH_AND_OUTDOORS.md`

## User-Facing Features

- Today's Shift Health Plan
- Next Recommended Break
- Hydration check-ins
- Outdoor/daylight minute tracking
- Eyes and posture prompts
- Nervous-system reset with optional faith prompt
- End-of-day downshift
- Weekly nature target
- Weekly Health Review
- Manager-safe Evidence Pack summary text
- Email Reminder Setup with copyable schedule, calendar text, and Google Apps Script prompt

## Reminder Defaults

Default shift days are Monday and Wednesday. Default shift time is 8:30am-5:00pm.

- 8:20am: pre-shift setup
- 9:20am: 20-20-20 eye break and water
- 10:30am: outdoor reset if possible
- 11:30am: posture, jaw, shoulders, water
- 12:30pm: lunch away from screen
- 2:15pm: outdoor walk or sunlight reset
- 3:30pm: water, stretch, eyes
- 4:45pm: end-of-day shutdown

The schedule can be edited in the Health & Outdoors settings section. Other shift days can also be enabled manually.

## Local Data Stored

Data is stored in browser localStorage under `avance-health-outdoors`.

The app stores simple wellbeing action data only:

- completedBreaks
- skippedBreaks
- hydrationCount
- outdoorMinutes
- movementBreaks
- eyeBreaks
- lunchAwayFromScreenCount
- shutdownCount
- urgentTicketModeCount
- lastBreakTime
- snoozedUntil
- notificationPermissionStatus
- preferredReminderCadence
- mondayWednesdayOnly
- notificationsEnabled
- quietModeUntil
- reminderSound

The app must not store client names, passwords, IP addresses, hostnames, screenshots, copied ticket text, private medical notes, or other sensitive operational data.

## Notification Behavior

- Browser notification permission is requested only after the user clicks `Enable health reminders`.
- If permission is granted, local browser notifications can be shown for due reminders.
- If permission is denied or unsupported, the app uses in-app banners.
- Reminder sound defaults to off.
- Quiet mode pauses reminders for 60 minutes during urgent ticket work.

## Email Reminder Design

No email is sent from the frontend. Phase 1 provides copy/export helpers only.

Future email sending would require a backend or automation service, such as:

- `/api/send-health-reminder`
- Google Apps Script
- Gmail automation
- a scheduled service

Any future implementation must keep secrets server-side and must not expose Gmail credentials or API tokens in client code.

## Build Verification

Command used:

```bash
npm run build
```

Result: TypeScript and Vite production build pass.

## Known Limitations

- Email reminders are not sent automatically.
- Notifications are local browser notifications only, not push server notifications.
- Browser notification behavior depends on browser permission settings.
- Health data is local to the current browser profile unless manually exported.

The app should feel calm, practical, and work-ready.

## Tone

- Brief and direct.
- Warm without being overly casual.
- No shame, guilt, or red failure language for normal misses.
- Prefer "reset", "review", "next action", and "keep going steadily".
- Keep faith prompts optional and workplace-appropriate.

## UX Principles

- Surface the next useful action quickly.
- Keep dashboards scannable.
- Use cards for repeated items and focused tools.
- Keep forms compact and clear.
- Preserve keyboard access.
- Use large enough tap targets for mobile.
- Avoid clutter during busy work states.

## Visual Principles

- High contrast text.
- Calm neutral surfaces.
- Clear headings.
- Consistent status chips.
- No red states for skipped health or learning actions.
- Support reduced motion.

## Accessibility Checklist

- Buttons and inputs are keyboard reachable.
- Focus states are visible.
- Headings follow a sensible order.
- Text does not depend on colour alone.
- Mobile layout remains usable without horizontal scrolling.

This guide describes a simple Avance shift routine.

## Start Of Shift

1. Open the app.
2. Check `Dashboard` for next shift context and open follow-ups.
3. Open `Avance Workday`.
4. Use the start-of-day checklist.
5. Set a generic focus, such as "triage queue", "follow-ups", or "documentation".
6. Check the `Healthy MSP Shift` panel for the next wellbeing action.

## During The Shift

- Use quick capture for generic notes, follow-ups, and learning.
- Use `Tasks` for actions that must survive the next shift gap.
- Use `Knowledge` and `Playbooks` for reusable, non-sensitive patterns.
- Use `Ticket Notes` to practise clean summaries without copying real ticket text.
- Use `Health & Outdoors` for water, outdoor time, eye breaks, movement, and shutdown prompts.

## Quiet Or Overwhelmed Moments

- Use Avance Workday's quiet-time PD suggestions when there is a small gap.
- Use "urgent ticket mode" in Health & Outdoors when reminders need to back off.
- Use the 2-minute reset when you need to return to one clear next action.

## End Of Shift

1. Review open tasks.
2. Capture any generic learning.
3. Update evidence where useful.
4. Use the Health & Outdoors shutdown prompt: close loops, note next actions, breathe, and let work stay at work.

## Privacy Reminder

Keep client details, credentials, IPs, hostnames, copied tickets, screenshots, and private medical notes out of the app.

Avance Work Companion is a local-first support and professional development app for Josh's ICT/MSP work rhythm at Avance.

## Purpose

- Help Josh start shifts calmly and quickly.
- Keep generic work context, follow-ups, learning, and evidence visible.
- Support sustainable Monday/Wednesday MSP work without storing client-sensitive material.

- Local-first by default.
- Fast capture over perfect documentation.
- Gentle prompts, not shame.
- Professional wording suitable for workplace use.
- Privacy before convenience.
- Practical PD that connects learning to real support habits.
- Calm, readable UI that works under pressure.

## Privacy Rules

Do not store:

- client names or company names
- passwords, API keys, recovery codes, or secrets
- IP addresses, hostnames, screenshots, copied ticket text, or private operational details
- private health diagnoses or medical notes

Use generic categories such as "M365 access request", "endpoint issue", "triage queue", or "documentation follow-up".

## Current Scope

- Dashboard
- Avance Workday
- Health & Outdoors
- Shift scheduler
- Tasks
- Work logs
- Knowledge
- Playbooks
- Time
- PD learning log
- MSP skills, scenarios, quiz, roadmap, ticket notes, communication practice, micro-learning, and Evidence Pack

## Success Metrics

- Josh can understand the next useful action within 60 seconds of opening the app.
- Busy-shift capture takes less than a minute.
- Follow-ups survive the gap between Monday and Wednesday shifts.
- Learning evidence is manager-safe and useful without revealing sensitive details.
- Health prompts support sustainability without interrupting urgent ticket work.

Use this checklist before release or deployment changes.

## Build

- Run `npm run build`.
- Confirm TypeScript and Vite complete successfully.

## Core Navigation

- Dashboard opens.
- Avance Workday opens.
- Health & Outdoors opens.
- MSP Skills, Scenarios, Ticket Notes, Evidence Pack, and Micro-Learning open.

## Local Persistence

- Create a task, refresh, and confirm it remains.
- Create a work log, refresh, and confirm it remains.
- Create a learning note, refresh, and confirm it remains.
- Export backup JSON from Dashboard.

## Workflows

- Dashboard shows next shift, open follow-ups, Healthy MSP Shift, and Quick Capture.
- Tasks survive shift transitions because they are stored in localStorage.
- Knowledge and Playbooks search by title, tags, checks, symptoms, and category.
- Time page shows billable totals and invoice preview.
- Quick Capture presets reduce typing during busy states.

## Health & Outdoors

- Notification permission is requested only after user click.
- Denied or unsupported notifications use in-app banners.
- Snooze works.
- Quiet mode works.
- Reset and export actions work.

## Privacy

- No client names, credentials, IPs, hostnames, screenshots, copied tickets, or private medical notes are required by any flow.

The app remains local-first. Sync is optional future work and should only be added if local backup/export is not enough.

## Preferred Order

1. Manual JSON backup and restore.
2. Private Vercel deployment with browser localStorage.
3. Optional Supabase sync after explicit opt-in.

## Requirements For Any Sync

- Keep client data, credentials, screenshots, IPs, hostnames, and copied tickets out of sync.
- Use server-side secrets only.
- Add export/delete controls before enabling sync.
- Make sync opt-in per browser profile.
- Keep Health & Outdoors data simple and non-medical.

## Candidate Data To Sync

- tasks
- work logs
- learning items
- knowledge entries
- playbooks
- progress state
- health action counts and reminder settings

## Data Not To Sync

- API keys
- passwords
- client-identifying details
- screenshots
- ticket exports
- private health or medical notes

- Email sending through `/api/send-health-reminder`.
- Direct Gmail or calendar API integrations.
- PSA/RMM integrations.

- Server-side secrets only.
- Opt-in for any cloud sync or external API.
- Export/delete controls before sync.
- No client names, passwords, IPs, hostnames, screenshots, copied tickets, or private medical notes.
